name: Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma
aliases: Punctate Keratoderma of the Palms and Soles

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of multiple discrete hyperkeratotic papules on the palms and soles
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Histological confirmation showing epidermal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis without epidermolytic changes
Exclusion of other forms of palmoplantar keratoderma by clinical and histological evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic hyperkeratotic papules on palms and soles with histopathological confirmation and exclusion of other keratodermas
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not routinely required

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermal hyperplasia and compact orthokeratosis
Negative fungal cultures in absence of secondary infection
genetic: Mutations in AAGAB gene reported in some familial cases
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic punctate keratotic papules
Family history consistent with inherited pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse thickening of entire palmoplantar skin rather than discrete papules
Earlier onset in infancy or childhood
Histology showing epidermolytic hyperkeratosis in some forms

redFlags: Rapid progression or ulceration of lesions
Severe pain disproportionate to lesion size
Signs of secondary infection such as purulence or systemic symptoms
